title: Metric evolution under Ricci flow
mathematical_role: Expose time-indexed metric evolution while keeping qualitative curvature encoding distinct from the geometry itself.
learning_objective: Read g(t) as the evolving metric, distinguish smoothing from localized curvature concentration, and recognize that a schematic curvature indicator is not a computed singularity.
literal_semantics: The displayed evolution equation is ∂g/∂t = −2 Ric(g).
The three panels are explicitly ordered t₀, t₁, t₂ to represent a time-indexed teaching sequence.
The qualitative curvature bars are a separate visual channel from the drawn metric mesh.
nonliteral_semantics: The surfaces are schematic teaching models, not literal three-manifolds or numerical Ricci-flow states.
Mesh spacing is not a metric or curvature scale.
The highlighted final region is not a computed singularity or theorem-certified canonical neighbourhood.
Curvature-bar lengths are qualitative and not measurements.

notes: The successor is a governed schematic reconstruction of the documentary explanation; analytic control remains imported theorem context.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG renderer v1
reproducibility_notes: No randomness or external service is used.
Run the generator from any checkout; output paths and bytes are deterministic under the recorded Python-standard-library contract.

accessibility.alt_text: Three time-indexed schematic geometries evolve under Ricci flow; a separate qualitative curvature channel grows toward a highlighted region, explicitly marked as not a computed singularity.
accessibility.long_description: The plate has three panels labelled t0, t1, and t2 beneath the Ricci-flow equation. Each panel shows a metric-like mesh on a changing surface. Beneath each surface is a separate qualitative curvature-magnitude bar. The final panel circles a region of interest. A boundary box states that the panels are not numerical Ricci-flow solutions or singularity certificates.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical reconstruction of the distinction between metric evolution, smoothing, and qualitative curvature concentration in the documentary Ricci-flow narrative.
not_claimed: Any proof of Hamilton-Perelman estimates or the Poincare theorem

supersession_reason: The successor makes time evolution and the separation between geometry and curvature encoding explicit while preserving the non-evidentiary boundary.
